transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main reason I’m here is because I can’t seem to stay on what I’m trying to do. Like, even when I really need to focus on something—like filling out an application or trying to get through some kind of task—I get pulled away by every little thing.

It can be a sound outside, like a car going by, or my phone lighting up, or even just some random thought that pops into my head. And then suddenly I’m doing something completely different, or I’m looking something up, or I’ve gotten up and walked away, and I don’t even realize I’ve gone off track until later. It’s like my brain keeps grabbing onto whatever comes near it, if that makes sense.

It’s frustrating because I’ll sit down meaning to do one thing, and then somehow a bunch of time passes and the original thing still isn’t done. That’s probably the biggest thing that made me come in.

Thinking back, do you remember having this same kind of trouble staying focused and getting easily distracted back when you were a kid, like in elementary school, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

Yeah, no, it definitely goes back. It’s not just something that started recently.

I remember in elementary school, teachers were always moving my seat around because I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, like blurting things out or whispering to whoever was next to me. And it wasn’t even always me trying to be bad or anything—I’d just think of something and say it, or I’d get pulled into whatever someone else was doing.

Homework was a big thing too. I’d forget to turn it in, or forget to bring it home, or I’d do it and then somehow it just wouldn’t make it back to school. And worksheets… I remember rushing through them just to be done, and then I’d have all these little mistakes that I probably could’ve caught if I slowed down. Teachers would write things like “slow down” or “check your work,” stuff like that.

So yeah, thinking back, it was there pretty early. I didn’t really have words for it then, but the same kind of problems were happening.
Aside from the trouble focusing, do you often find yourself feeling excessively worried or on edge about various things in your daily life, even when there's no clear reason to be?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m walking around constantly worried about everything for no reason, if that’s what you mean.

Like, I get stressed when I’m behind on something or when I know I forgot something important, but that feels more tied to what’s happening, not like this general dread all the time. I’m trying to think… I don’t really notice myself being on edge about a bunch of different things for no clear reason. It’s more that my mind is all over the place, and then I get frustrated or stressed because of the mess that creates.

So… yeah, I’m not sure I’d describe it as excessive worry exactly. I can worry, obviously, but I don’t think that’s the main thing.
Do you currently use alcohol, cannabis, or any other recreational drugs, and if so, how often?

Um… I’m not totally sure how to answer, because I don’t really have anything specific to report there. Like, I’m not coming in because of alcohol or weed or anything like that.

I guess when you say “currently use,” do you mean like regular use, or ever at all, or just anything recently? Because I don’t want to answer the wrong version of the question. I haven’t really noticed that as being a factor in what’s going on, if that makes sense. It’s not something I’ve been tracking closely.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still for long periods, like in meetings or while watching a movie?

Yeah, definitely. I notice it mostly when I’m sitting with someone and I’m supposed to just be listening or staying still. My leg will be bouncing the whole time, or I’ll be clicking a pen without even thinking about it. Sometimes I’m messing with my keys in my pocket or flipping them around in my hand, and I don’t even realize I’m doing it until someone looks at me or I notice the sound.

It’s not always like I feel like I’m going to jump out of my seat, exactly, but my body is usually doing something. Like sitting still feels… I don’t know, kind of unnatural after a while. If there’s something in front of me, I’ll usually end up fiddling with it.
Do you often find yourself interrupting people mid-sentence, blurting out answers or comments before someone finishes speaking, or having a hard time waiting your turn in conversations or lines?

Yeah… I do that. Probably more than I realize, honestly.

Like with my mom especially, she’ll be in the middle of explaining something and I already think I know where she’s going with it, so I jump in and answer before she’s actually finished. And then sometimes it turns out I didn’t even let her get to the main point, so she gets annoyed, which… fair. I’m not trying to be rude, it’s just the response kind of pops into my head and I say it before I’ve really decided to say it.

It happens with the counselor too. They’ll ask something or start making a point, and I’ll cut in because I suddenly have an answer or a thought and it feels like if I don’t say it right then, I’ll lose it. Then I realize I interrupted, and I’m like, “Sorry, go ahead,” but by then I’ve already done it.

So yeah, waiting my turn in a conversation can be hard. Not because I don’t care what they’re saying, more like my mouth gets ahead of me.
